system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Playbook vs Seller Update + Disclosure Letter dated 22 Sept 2026 (now ~6 weeks stale as at 4 Nov 2026)

**Headline:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. It (i) lands on our *conditional fallbacks* on cap and time limit without any Amelia Frost authority having been given, (ii) collapses Fundamental/Title, Tax and IP into the general regime, (iii) contains no fraud carve-out and extends limitations/non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature", and (iv) leaves every pre-Completion deliverable (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) unresolved. Helpfully, the Disclosure Letter itself candidly admits most of those gaps – we should use its own words against the Seller Update.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is only our conditional fallback and no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft exists, so we have no mandate to accept it.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject all three elements; revert to playbook figures and tipping structure.** The Seller's numbers are 5x ours and the deductible mechanic would permanently strand AUD 250,000 of loss – a hidden price reduction.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; hold 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the default rule would quietly import general-regime limits into Title/Tax/IP/indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; this is a walk-away-grade point.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m if we do not actually own the company – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct carve-out anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable.
- **Recommendation:** **Non-negotiable: insert the carve-out and narrow cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 accordingly.** No one on our side has authority to waive this, and a non-reliance clause purporting to cover fraud is unlikely to be enforceable in NSW anyway – so the Seller loses nothing legitimate by conceding it.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire indexed data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only (matters disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope); no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DL 1.1–1.2 and the Schedule 7 mechanism; require a "fairly disclosed" standard and a specific disclosure schedule.** Blanket data-room disclosure converts every warranty into a warranty that we read everything, and the letter is also stale – require a bring-down to Completion with no new disclosures permitted against signed warranties.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must (a) attach to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, (b) have a seller-side counterpart of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and (c) never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3 in full.** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test that, combined with SPA-N-006, would make the warranties practically unclaimable.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours only; consent "treated as satisfied" on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 admits no final written consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied are in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (i) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent under cl 11.2/11.3 and (ii) documentary evidence that those conditions are met, both delivered before Completion; Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "satisfied on delivery" deeming and reasonable-endeavours standard; redraft as a hard CP with evidence of condition satisfaction.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, and a consent that is delivered but conditional on unmet terms is not a consent.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge of security included.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark, repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow, and executed releases/discharges of all security delivered at Completion (consistent with debt-free/cash-free).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-Completion release; require payout + direct repayment + releases as Completion deliverables.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists – and the facility's change-of-control clause 8.1 is otherwise a live default risk from minute one.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals if any) either (a) a specific line item in the funds flow paid by/deducted from the Seller, or (b) treated as Debt/transaction cost in the price adjustment; Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require express line item or seller funding, with grossed-up on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the liability crystallises in the Company post-Completion and we pay it.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4 confirms transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 shown open on DD-010 is not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering all loss from any failure of title to, or encumbrance over, the SOW3 (and any other Ironquay) Project Materials, including re-procurement, licence fees and third-party claims – not just the fee amount; preserve the cure route (pay SOW3 fees pre-Completion and obtain confirmatory assignment).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and add a pre-Completion cure deliverable (paid receipt + confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay).** The exposure is loss of ownership of deliverables, not merely a AUD 180,000 invoice – and we should not treat the AUD 180,000 as either confirmed owed or confirmed paid until bank-verified.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); access, scope and notification obligations not established; no breach characterisation, no loss figure.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve all logs/evidence, complete the investigation, and provide written updates; warranty that the disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion; a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party) uncapped by the general basket. Do not demand or concede any number.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require preservation, investigation, updates and a specific indemnity, without quantifying.** On the current record there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand in either direction, so the correct response is process and risk allocation, not a price adjustment.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each are "ordinary-course operating costs". DL 8 is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course and says DD-008/DD-011 must be read together for timing/scope.
- **Buyer wants:** Full assessment – timing, whether committed/terminable, whether accrued or prepaid at the locked-box/completion accounts date, and whether a change-of-control or auto-renewal trigger exists – before accepting any classification.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the Seller's characterisation but do not demand a Debt classification or price deduction yet; raise a targeted DD request.** Our playbook treats this as an assessment item, and the Seller's own letter concedes it has not established the facts needed for either side's characterisation.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; the cl 12.3/13 default that any limitation applies to all Claims; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 applied to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/price-adjustment and covenant/indemnity claims each in their own expressly separate regime; general limitations apply only where expressly stated; no override language.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete all three override mechanisms and insert an express "limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims unless stated" clause.** The Seller has used three different drafting routes to achieve one result – a single 20%/18-month cap on everything – and each must be closed off individually.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes this merely "identifies the source relied on" and does not state the Buyer has verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical company search, executed share certificates, signed and dated register with transfer history, PPSR search over the shares and the Company, Seller board/shareholder authorisations, and confirmation of no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DD-012 as sufficient; commission independent title/encumbrance/authority searches now and make clean results a Completion deliverable.** An internal register supplied by the Seller is the thing being warranted, not proof of it.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both remain OPEN and negotiated separately – dedicated Tax and IP warranty sets, separate caps/time limits (tax typically to statutory review periods), and a tax indemnity. We do not seek unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items and table separate schedules.** Nothing has been agreed, and folding them into the general regime would be a concession made by silence.

---

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. **Deal-structure items:** SPA-N-005 (fraud), SPA-N-004 (Title regime), SPA-N-014 (category separation) – these go to whether the warranties are worth anything.
2. **Completion deliverables:** SPA-N-008 (Bluefen), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark), SPA-N-010 (bonuses), SPA-N-015 (title evidence), SPA-N-011 (Ironquay cure).
3. **Economic limitations:** SPA-N-001, -002, -003 – hold playbook; flag to Amelia Frost that the Seller has pre-emptively landed on our fallbacks, so any later move requires her written authority identifying the draft.
4. **Disclosure mechanics:** SPA-N-006, -007 – delete blanket disclosure/knowledge; require bring-down given the letter is dated 22 Sept 2026.
5. **DD follow-ups:** SPA-N-012, -013, -016 – process and information requests, no numbers conceded.

**Two further points to note:** (a) DL 1.4's blanket non-admission should be accepted as standard but with an express statement that it does not qualify the warranties or the specific indemnities; (b) DD-007 (lease notification) and DD-009 (Mossvale) are not on the issue list but should be confirmed as notice-only items and swept into a pre-Completion notification covenant.
=== END ADVICE ===
